items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: Cosmo and I was the first black, white to get a sleeping bird train from here in New Orleans... I stayed in New York. The only time I saw Cosmo was when I was in the studio... The deal was made then that with Cosmo... They recorded the tune

ctx.x: Yeah. Was it a big hit in New Orleans?

Yeah, well, it was a big hit in New Orleans. In fact, I have requests for it now. I don't remember that song. But it's in this album. Uh-huh, yeah. And, you know, I listened to, I listened to the record and, and it sound better now than it did then because I think they were able to take some hiss out and you get a little bit better quality of what you can hear now than a long time ago. But I used to hate that, you know, after, later on I listened to that bad sound. See, because in recording, Cosmo would look up…
Okay, there was another song called Lavinia. Lavinia.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Cosmos' (likely a studio or engineer) in the context of recording sessions ('Cosmos would luck up and get one...'), but does not describe a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction with a specific individual named Cosmos beyond professional proximity to

ctx.x: Oh, the going across the river, was that done at Cosmos and for some reason it doesn't... I'm going across that river? Yeah. Oh, you haven't done that Cosmos? I was just wondering, for some reason it didn't sound... Sometimes Cosmos Studio sound sort of changes at different periods.

Cosmos would luck up and get one, you know, and then he'd miss, and then he'd luck up and get another. But when he was on Dumaine Street, see that was when we all, everything sounded like it was in a little box, although the fat man came out of there. And Jewel King, three times seven, and a lot of other things. But then he moved on Governor Nichols. Right. Okay, this was when the studio was much bigger, you know, and I think this was when the sound kind of evolved to be better. And I did a lot of things over…
